message.content: {"summary":"You produced a well-structured, balanced report with a justified Not Ship recommendation. Your introduction and stakeholder analysis are excellent, and your argument structure is compelling. To improve, you need stakeholder-specific decision guidance, quantitative evidence, and required visual elements.","next_steps":["For C2 Excellent: in DISCUSSION and The Most Ethical Path, add explicit recommendations for Rachel, her company, the chip contractor, and the health department, not just Rachel.","For C4 Excellent: add quantitative evidence for costs, failure rates or recall impacts alongside your Engineers Australia, HSSIB and Volkswagen case studies.","For C5 Very Good/Excellent: add at least two visual elements, e.g., stakeholder impact matrix and risk trade-off table, cited in-text."],"criteria":{"C1":"You excelled here. In INTRODUCTION you identified public safety, integrity, reputation and QA pressure, linked to competitive design pressure, and listed all stakeholders including end-users. Keep this depth for future tasks.","C2":"You built objective for/against arguments with trade-offs in DISCUSSION: To Ship or Not to Ship. For Excellent, you need recommendations for several stakeholders, not just a single Not Ship conclusion for Rachel.","C3":"Your logic from pros to cons to The Most Ethical Path is compelling and your CONCLUSION is well-supported. You showed systematic understanding of harm severity to end-users and company-wide integrity.","C4":"You substantiated well with Engineers Australia Code, HSSIB/BBC and CNBC sources. To reach Excellent, add quantitative data such as failure probability, cost of recall, or NHS impact stats alongside qualitative cases.","C5":"Your ABSTRACT, INTRODUCTION, body and CONCLUSION are fluent with consistent referencing. To move to Good or higher, you must include visual elements (figures/tables) correctly labeled and referenced in text, as rubric requires."}}
